classification.difficultyReason: Derive two triangle areas from fractional bases, subtract their combined area from the rectangle, and simplify the area ratio.

inlines.text: The base of triangle A is half the length of the rectangle.
The base of triangle B is three quarters of the length of the rectangle.
Find the ratio of the unshaded area to the shaded area.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 9 rectangle and its external dimensions
spec.description: Rectangle partitioned into two unshaded triangles A and B and three light-purple shaded regions. Dimensions are 8 cm horizontally and 2 cm vertically.
spec.mathematics: Triangle A has a bottom-edge base of 4 cm. Triangle B has a top-edge base of 6 cm. Both have perpendicular height 2 cm. Their interiors are disjoint. Coordinates encode the supplied base relationships and source topology; the position of B's bottom vertex preserves the source arrangement without adding a numerical given.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied geometry, triangle names and rectangle dimensions are visible; no calculated areas or ratio.

answer.short:
Triangle A: $4\text{ cm}^2$. Triangle B: $6\text{ cm}^2$.

Unshaded to shaded $=5:3$.
answer.worked:
Both triangles have height $2\text{ cm}$.

$$\begin{align*}
\text{Base of A}&=\tfrac12\times8=4\text{ cm}\\
\text{Base of B}&=\tfrac34\times8=6\text{ cm}\\
\text{Area of A}&=\tfrac12\times4\times2=4\text{ cm}^2\\
\text{Area of B}&=\tfrac12\times6\times2=6\text{ cm}^2\\
\text{Unshaded area}&=4+6=10\text{ cm}^2\\
\text{Rectangle area}&=8\times2=16\text{ cm}^2\\
\text{Shaded area}&=16-10=6\text{ cm}^2\\
\text{Unshaded : shaded}&=10:6\\
\text{Unshaded : shaded}&=5:3
\end{align*}$$
